name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to gain initial access, often abusing software bugs, misconfigurations, or unpatched vulnerabilities in web servers, databases, and network services.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries, interacting with shells such as bash, PowerShell, and cmd to control a system.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute commands and scripts, leveraging its access to the Windows API and ability to download and run code in memory.

name: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution, often via sh or bash to control a system and run other software.

name: JavaScript
description: Adversaries abuse JavaScript engines and runtimes to execute behaviors, including server-side Node.js execution and browser-side script in cross-site scripting attacks.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications such as browsers and document readers to execute code, typically after a user opens malicious content.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges, abusing programming errors in a program, service, or the operating-system kernel to run code in a higher-privileged context.

name: Exploitation for Credential Access
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to collect credentials, abusing programming errors to expose or extract credential material from memory or storage.

name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
description: Adversaries exploit a system or application vulnerability to bypass security features, disabling or circumventing defensive controls to evade detection.

name: Exploitation of Remote Services
description: Adversaries exploit remote services to move laterally inside a network, abusing unpatched services such as SMB, RDP, and database servers to gain access to other internal systems.

name: Web Shell
description: Adversaries deploy a web shell on a compromised web server to establish persistent access, using a script that allows arbitrary command execution through web requests.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain initial access, persistence, privilege escalation, or defense evasion, blending in with legitimate activity.

name: Unsecured Credentials
description: Adversaries search compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials, including those in files, environment variables, registry keys, and source code.

name: Credentials In Files
description: Adversaries search local file systems and remote file shares for files containing insecurely stored credentials, such as configuration files and source code.

name: Private Keys
description: Adversaries search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials, enabling decryption, signing, or authentication as the victim.

name: Group Policy Preferences
description: Adversaries retrieve passwords embedded in Group Policy Preferences XML files, which were historically encrypted with a publicly known key.

name: Network Sniffing
description: Adversaries sniff network traffic to capture information, including credentials transmitted over cleartext or weakly encrypted protocols.

name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
description: Adversaries position themselves between two networked devices to support follow-on behaviors such as transmitted-data manipulation and credential interception.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries use brute-force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained, including password guessing and credential stuffing.

name: Forge Web Credentials
description: Adversaries forge credential material such as session cookies and authentication tokens to gain access to web applications and services.

name: Modify Authentication Process
description: Adversaries modify authentication mechanisms and processes to access credentials or enable unwarranted access to accounts, bypassing intended authentication controls.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service
description: Adversaries perform endpoint denial-of-service attacks to degrade or block the availability of services, exhausting the resources of the system hosting the service.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries perform network denial-of-service attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources by exhausting network bandwidth.

name: Data from Information Repositories
description: Adversaries leverage information repositories such as wikis, code repositories, and ticketing systems to mine valuable information, including credentials and sensitive data.

name: Data from Local System
description: Adversaries search local system sources such as file systems and configuration files to find sensitive files of interest prior to exfiltration.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate files and directories or search specific locations of a host or network share for specific information within a file system.

name: Path Traversal Discovery
description: Adversaries abuse path traversal sequences to escape an intended directory and read files outside the application's scope.

name: Data Manipulation
description: Adversaries insert, delete, or manipulate data to influence outcomes, hide activity, or affect the integrity of business processes and decisions.

name: Data Destruction
description: Adversaries destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers to interrupt availability of systems, services, and network resources.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability, as performed by ransomware.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
description: Adversaries manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
description: Adversaries manipulate software dependencies and development tools prior to receipt by a final consumer, embedding malicious code in upstream packages.

name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
description: Adversaries manipulate application software prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise, inserting backdoors into legitimate products.

name: Implant Internal Image
description: Adversaries implant cloud or container images with malicious code to establish persistence after gaining access to an environment.

name: Deploy Container
description: Adversaries deploy a container into an environment to facilitate execution or evade defenses, sometimes deploying images configured without network rules or security tooling.

name: Escape to Host
description: Adversaries break out of a container to gain access to the underlying host, abusing misconfigurations or vulnerabilities in the container runtime.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries communicate using OSI application-layer protocols such as HTTP and DNS to blend command-and-control traffic with existing network activity.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command-and-control channel, encoding stolen data into normal communications.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
description: Adversaries use obfuscated or encoded information that is decoded at runtime to evade static analysis and detection.

name: Hijack Execution Flow
description: Adversaries execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way operating systems run programs, abusing search-order and path weaknesses.

name: Server Software Component
description: Adversaries abuse legitimate extensible development features of servers to establish persistent access to systems, installing malicious components.

name: Remote Access Software
description: Adversaries use legitimate remote-access tools to establish an interactive command-and-control channel within a network.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create an account to maintain access to victim systems, establishing persistence without requiring persistent remote-access tools.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges to gain higher-level permissions, abusing sudo, setuid binaries, and similar controls.

name: Modify Registry
description: Adversaries interact with the Windows Registry to hide configuration information, remove information as part of cleanup, or as part of other techniques.

name: Application or System Exploitation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities that can cause an application or system to crash and deny the availability of services.

name: Gather Victim Host Information
description: Adversaries gather information about the victim's hosts that can be used during targeting, including details exposed through verbose errors and banners.

name: Code Repositories
description: Adversaries leverage code repositories to collect valuable information, including credentials and proprietary source code committed in plaintext.

name: Steal Web Session Cookie
description: Adversaries steal web application or service session cookies and use them to gain access to applications or Internet services as an authenticated user without needing credentials.

name: Event Triggered Execution
description: Adversaries establish persistence using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events, abusing deserialization and callback handlers.
